catalog_quote: 2.1.3 SUPRASEGMENTAL PHONEMES. 2.1.3.1 STRESS. Stress is phonemic. Compare: (7) /xuⁿdó/ foot, /xúⁿdo/ meat; (8) /réᵑge/ red, /reᵑgé/ penis. [p.9] ... Lexical items each have their own (in Kombai unpredictable) main word stress but functors tend to be unstressed. The form reduction of relational nouns and verbs follows this stress-reduction. [p.89] ... The modifying stem always precedes the modified stem in the compound noun, for example, wodei 'river' and bei 'bank' may be combined to become wodeibei 'riverbank'; the modifying stem attracts the main word stress in these compounds. [p.34] || de Vries 2020:14, sec.2.3.3 'Kombai syllables, words, stress': There is one syllable type in Kombai (C)V. The canonical word form is (C)V.(CV) Kombai has contrastive stress in the form of a pitch accent on the prominent syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Kombai is lexically contrastive (phonemic) and not predictable from position: disyllables contrast initial vs final stress (xúⁿdo 'meat' vs xuⁿdó 'foot'; réᵑge 'red' vs reᵑgé 'penis'). Each lexical item carries its own main stress; function words (relators/functors) tend to be unstressed; in modifier-head compound nouns the first (modifying) stem takes main stress. The author later (2020) characterises the realisation as a pitch accent on the prominent syllable. No default/elsewhere position is given.
new_statements.exceptions: None as such (no default rule to have exceptions to); functors tend to be unstressed and reduce; compound nouns: modifying stem stressed, coordinate compounds not discussed for Kombai in 1993.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level ('main word stress' of lexical items; citation forms in minimal pairs). Phrase-level remark only that cliticised relators/functors are unstressed. de Vries 2020 calls it 'contrastive stress in the form of a pitch accent' -- a reviewer may prefer the 'pitch-accent' reading label; the primary 1993 text says 'stress is phonemic' and 'unpredictable'.
new_statements.identity_note: de Vries 1993 describes Central Kombai (villages Wanggemalo and Yaniruma, Kouh sub-district), one of three main dialects he names (Central Kombai, Wanggom, Tayan); Glottolog komb1274 = Kombai [tyn] as a whole. Wanggom is sometimes listed separately (ISO wng, Glottolog wang1299 'Wanggom'); the statement here is for Central Kombai.

sources.note: Ch.2 'Kombai phonemes', sec.2.1.3 Suprasegmental phonemes, 2.1.3.1 Stress (p.9): 'Stress is phonemic', with minimal pairs /xuⁿdó/ 'foot' vs /xúⁿdo/ 'meat', /réᵑge/ 'red' vs /reᵑgé/ 'penis'. p.34: in modifier-modified compound nouns the modifying (first) stem attracts main word stress. p.89: 'Lexical items each have their own (in Kombai unpredictable) main word stress but functors tend to be unstressed.' No default position, no secondary stress, no tone.
